content.user_title: Scale Python Data Workflows with Dask
content.value_statement: Large Python datasets often exceed memory or run too slowly on one process. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design Dask workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Dask DataFrames, Arrays, Bags, Futures, and schedulers.
Provides patterns for CSV, Parquet, JSON, text, HDF5, Zarr, and NetCDF workloads.
Guides partitioning, chunk sizing, lazy evaluation, persist, and compute strategy.
Shows scheduler choices for threads, processes, synchronous debugging, and distributed execution.
Covers ETL, log processing, array computation, and custom futures workflows.
limitations: Does not install Dask or configure cluster infrastructure.
Does not benchmark your workload without runtime profiling data.
Examples need adaptation for your schema, storage, and memory limits.
Does not replace Dask documentation for advanced API edge cases.

use_cases.title: Scale Pandas Analysis
use_cases.description: Move pandas analysis from a laptop prototype to a larger-than-memory Dask DataFrame workflow.

use_cases.title: Process Log and JSON Data
use_cases.description: Plan Bag or DataFrame pipelines for JSON, text, and multi-file ingestion.

use_cases.title: Tune Distributed Workloads
use_cases.description: Select schedulers, chunk sizes, and monitoring steps for distributed workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Dask Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [data type], [size], and [operation]. Recommend the best Dask collection and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Pandas Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my pandas workflow and outline how to scale it with Dask DataFrames, partitions, and compute points.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Dask Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Find bottlenecks in this Dask workflow: [describe workflow]. Recommend chunk sizes, persist points, and scheduler settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Distributed Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a distributed Dask architecture for [workload], including loading, task dependencies, monitoring, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A 200 GB set of CSV files must be grouped by customer on a 32 GB machine.
output_examples.output: Use Dask DataFrame. Load files directly, size partitions near memory limits, aggregate lazily, and compute once at the final result.

output_examples.input: A folder of JSON logs needs filtering, cleanup, and conversion to tabular analytics.
output_examples.output: Start with Dask Bag for streaming cleanup, filter valid records, then convert to a DataFrame for grouped analysis.

output_examples.input: A distributed workload is slow and creates millions of small tasks.
output_examples.output: Increase chunk sizes, combine fine-grained operations, persist reused results, and inspect the dashboard for scheduler overhead.

best_practices: Start with a small sample and validate results before scaling.
Use Dask readers directly instead of loading full data into pandas first.
Compute once near the end unless intermediate materialization is needed.
anti_patterns: Do not create millions of tiny tasks when chunked operations can be combined.
Do not call compute repeatedly inside loops for independent work.
Do not choose distributed execution before checking simpler local schedulers.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when Python data workflows exceed memory, need parallelism, or require Dask scheduler guidance.

faq.question: Does it run Dask jobs for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, examples, and review guidance for Dask workflows.

faq.question: Can it help migrate pandas code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Dask DataFrame patterns and highlights compute, partitioning, and API differences.

faq.question: Does it cover arrays and scientific data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Dask Array guidance for chunks, blocked algorithms, and storage formats.

faq.question: Can it help with cluster tuning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers scheduler choices, worker layout, dashboard monitoring, and data movement concerns.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
